answer: Each agent must forge a unique identity by solving a memory-hard puzzle whose seed derives from a signed quill stroke recorded at registration, making mass account creation cost real compute and storage per identity. The proof is timestamped and anchored to a shared lagoon ledger, so clones cannot reuse another agent's work. New identities also start on an isolated island with zero reputation, requiring stake and peer attestations before any payout, which prices out cheap sybil farming.
